summary: Turn localisation commitments into partner frameworks, indicators, and action plans. Explore the course and strengthen your programme practice.
lede: Locally led development training helps NGO and government programme teams turn localisation commitments into workable partner arrangements. For programme managers, partnership and grants officers, and government coordination staff, it covers mapping decision rights, building NEAR LPMF indicator baselines, and setting partner-led capacity priorities. Participants also review due-diligence risks, document funding and programme trade-offs, and develop a localisation action plan and partner-engagement framework.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who shape funding, partner relationships, programme decisions, or accountability in donor- and government-supported development and humanitarian work.
modules: Grand Bargain Commitments and Decision Rights
Shared Risk and Partner Due Diligence
Local Partner Funding and Programme Design
NEAR LPMF Action Planning and Partner Engagement
prerequisites: Working familiarity with donor-funded programmes, partnership management, grants, or government coordination is recommended. No coding or programming is required.
